text: Tie their wrists loosely with a soft scarf. Quick-release knot, scissors in reach, and check they can slip free. Then take your time.
aftercare: Untie them gently, rub their wrists, and ask what felt best.

text: Touch everywhere except where they want it most, until they ask nicely. You get to define 'nicely.'
aftercare: Give them exactly what they asked for, then hold them until they're calm again.

text: Scratch their back slowly, light to firm. They call out 'more' or 'less.' Keep it gentle enough that nothing lingers.
aftercare: Smooth lotion along every path you scratched.

text: Negotiate a spanking first: where, how firm, how many. Count them out loud together. Stop the instant the safeword lands.
aftercare: Rub the spot soothingly and tell them how much you trust them.

text: Blindfold on. Run five textures over their skin: silk, fur, something cool and metal, a soft brush, your lips. They rank them.
aftercare: Let them do the same to you, then compare your top picks.

text: Drag an ice cube slowly down their spine. Chase every drop with a warm kiss.
aftercare: Dry them off with a warm towel and keep them wrapped in it.

text: Secretly signal: soft ties tonight? Quick-release knots, scissors nearby, safeword ready. It only happens if everyone says yes.
aftercare: Release them slowly, massage where the ties were, and tell them what their trust felt like.

text: Blindfold and soft ties together, quick release in reach. They can't see or reach you. Tell them everything you're about to do, then do it.
aftercare: Unwrap them like a gift, then hold them until they're ready to talk.

text: Bring them right to the edge, then stop. Three times. On the fourth, they decide what happens.
aftercare: Bring them water, brush their hair back, and tell them they were incredible.

text: Pin their wrists gently above their head with one hand. Explore with the other. Let go the instant they ask.
aftercare: Kiss each wrist, then lace your fingers through theirs.

text: Sensory overload: blindfold, slow music, ice in one of your hands, a feather in the other. Ask 'color?' every few minutes.
aftercare: Take it all away one sense at a time, then finish with a long, quiet hug.

text: Strangers at a bar: each of you invents a name, a job, and one secret. Meet across the room and try to pick each other up.
aftercare: Drop character with a real kiss and tell them your favorite line of theirs.

text: One of you writes a very specific job title; the other writes three 'qualifications.' Hold the interview. Hire only if truly convinced.
aftercare: Give them a glowing performance review: three things they did that you loved.

text: The masseuse: agree on the menu beforehand. One books the deluxe treatment; the other decides, within the menu, what's included.
aftercare: Swap roles for a five-minute shoulder rub with no agenda at all.

text: Consensual boss and new hire, both adults, both very into it. Write the office rules together first, then hold a 'performance review.'
aftercare: Clock out together: comfy clothes, a snack, and a debrief.

text: Consensual royal and bodyguard. Decide together beforehand: who's sworn to protect whom, and which forbidden line gets crossed tonight?
aftercare: Out of character, tell them one moment that felt truly romantic.

text: Write a scene on three index cards: beginning, middle, end. Swap cards and act out your partner's version.
aftercare: Keep the cards, and tell them which line made you blush most.

text: Photographer and model. Each writes one pose the other may request. Run a shoot with no camera, only direction and praise.
aftercare: Tell them one 'shot' you'll be replaying in your head all week.

text: Each of you writes a secret scene on a card. Swap and read silently. Signal yes or no. You play it only if everyone says yes.
aftercare: Whatever the answer, thank them for trusting you with that card.

text: Rival spies, one consensual interrogation. Agree first on the secret, the limits, and the safeword. Extract the secret using only your mouth.
aftercare: Confess your own secret was always 'I adore you,' then hold them close.

text: Room service: write a menu of very adult offerings together. One orders; the other delivers. The tip is negotiable.
aftercare: Order a real snack together afterward and eat it in bed.

text: Celebrity and superfan, both adults, both entirely willing. Decide beforehand how far the meet-and-greet goes. Then let it go there.
aftercare: Remind them they're your favorite person, no costume required.

text: The genie: your partner writes three wishes beforehand, within limits you've agreed on. Grant them one at a time, fully in character.
aftercare: Grant one bonus wish after: a cuddle of any length they choose.

text: How to play   Set your heat.  Everyone picks a max heat, 1 to 5. The table plays at the  lowest  number picked. No one has to say why.   Take turns.  Draw, read it out loud, then choose:  do it  now,  claim it  for later, or  skip it . Skipping is always free.   Score Sparks.  The number in the corner is what the card is worth. First to the goal catches fire.

Sparks   Quick night:  first to 25.  Long night:  50.  Season:  keep a running total for a month.   The Woodpile.  Big cards (Wildfire, Slow Burn) are usually claimed now and done later. Keep them face up in front of you. They score when you complete them.   Match cards.  Everyone votes in secret. If everyone says yes, everyone does it and everyone scores  double .   Wild cards  bend the rules. Follow what they say.

Consent & care   Every card is optional.  Skip any card, any time, no reason given, no penalty, no eyebrows.   "Cool it."  Anyone can say it. The heat cap drops by one for the rest of the game.   "Ember out."  Anyone can say it. The game ends right there and you go get water, snacks, and a hug.  A yes tonight is not a yes forever. Check in like it's part of the game, because it is.

The Pot   Optional, and fun.  Before a Season starts, everyone puts the same amount into a jar. $20, $100, whatever feels right.   At the end,  the player with the most Sparks picks how the whole pot gets spent, from a wish list you all wrote together: a hotel night, a class, a dinner you've been eyeing.   The catch:  the player with the fewest Sparks has to plan it. Everyone goes. Everybody wins, someone just wins a little more.
